candidate_mechanisms.description: During provider processing, the buggy builder inserts a factory into its declared scope registry. A later cross-scope override updates the final processed-factory mapping but leaves the earlier per-scope entry stale. Request-scope lookup therefore returns 1 and shadows the later APP-scoped override 42.
candidate_mechanisms.testable_prediction: A fresh container with REQUEST int=1 followed by APP int=42 will resolve 1 on the buggy base; after deferring registry construction until all providers are processed, the same lookup resolves 42.

candidate_mechanisms.description: The observed value is caused by ordinary current-scope-before-parent lookup semantics rather than a stale registry entry.
candidate_mechanisms.testable_prediction: Without a stale local registration, parent fallback would return the APP-scoped value 42; a locally registered current-scope factory would ordinarily shadow the parent.

candidate_mechanisms.description: The consumer factory or container cache captured an earlier value independently of registry population.
candidate_mechanisms.testable_prediction: If consumer binding/cache is causal, the wrong value should remain explainable without a stale request-scope factory entry, potentially differing between direct get(int) resolution and resolving the Interactor.

gold_standard.technical_rationale: The pinned base reproducer and all eight frozen dataset selectors fail on the buggy base and pass on the fixed revision. The buggy builder writes to the scope registry during provider processing, before later overrides are complete; the fixed builder defers registry population and builds from the final processed-factory map. The independent reproducer changes the resolved value from 1 to the expected 42.

E1.semantic_rationale: E2 is retained unchanged. The buggy builder inserts each factory into the registry for its own scope during provider processing; the fixed builder defers registry population and builds from the final processed-factory map. The upstream cross-scope regression test asserts later provider precedence. This explains the stale REQUEST registration and distinguishes it from ordinary scope-chain precedence. Only G1 survives, as explicitly approved by the project lead.

E2.semantic_rationale: E3 is retained unchanged. The fresh-container reproducer and base lookup path show local cache then current-scope registry before parent fallback; direct registry lookup is from the local factory map. A prior consumer capture or cached int is not explanatory (A2 eliminated). E2 still does not reveal why the REQUEST registry holds the old factory, so G1 and A1 survive.

E3.semantic_rationale: Project-lead-approved E3 tier: the reported symptom and exact base/fix outputs establish the cross-scope override failure, but reveal no internal resolution path. G1, ordinary scope-chain precedence, and consumer/cache behavior remain competing mechanisms. Execution logs include both the independent issue reproducer and all eight exact dataset FAIL_TO_PASS selectors.

buggy_baseline.failure_signature: AssertionError: 'geodes_s3' not found in the mapping parsed from eodag/resources/user_conf_template.yml; the surviving geodes credentials are AWS fields.

candidate_mechanisms.description: The packaged YAML template contains two top-level mappings named geodes; ordinary YAML mapping parsing retains the later AWS-credential mapping, overwriting the earlier public API-key mapping and producing no distinct geodes_s3 mapping.
candidate_mechanisms.testable_prediction: On the exact buggy base, yaml.safe_load of the packaged template yields no geodes_s3 key and the surviving geodes credentials are AWS fields; renaming the second key to geodes_s3 preserves both mappings on the fixed revision.

candidate_mechanisms.description: A wrong template or installed-source revision is loaded, rather than the pinned packaged user_conf_template.yml under review.
candidate_mechanisms.testable_prediction: Inspecting and loading the exact pinned packaged template may not reproduce the observed configuration if the test/runtime actually resolves a different template or installed source revision.

candidate_mechanisms.description: A separate provider-registration or plugin-discovery failure causes the missing geodes_s3 provider independently of the duplicate YAML mapping.
candidate_mechanisms.testable_prediction: Even with distinct geodes and geodes_s3 mappings, provider registration/plugin discovery would still omit geodes_s3 from the application's supported provider mapping.

candidate_mechanisms.description: A generated or user-specific configuration override independently changes provider credentials and causes the public Geodes credential mismatch.
candidate_mechanisms.testable_prediction: The same credential mismatch would persist when the packaged template parses into two distinct provider mappings but an overriding generated/user-specific configuration is applied.

gold_standard.technical_rationale: The exact buggy template has two top-level geodes mappings. yaml.safe_load retains the later AWS credential mapping, overwriting the public API-key mapping and leaving no separate geodes_s3 mapping. The exact base fixture helper loads this packaged template with yaml.safe_load and iterates the provider mapping. PR #1536 renames the second mapping to geodes_s3. The independent YAML reproducer and both frozen issue-aligned dataset selectors fail on the exact buggy base and pass on the exact fixed revision. The separate StacListAssets change and related issue #1517 are excluded from this case's gold.

E3.semantic_rationale: Issue narrative alone does not establish the exact pinned parser output or the application's packaged-template fixture/loading path; all four predeclared explanations remain viable.

E2.semantic_rationale: The exact pinned YAML parse result shows duplicate-key collapse, removing the wrong-template/source-revision alternative A1. The E2 packet still does not establish the in-repository packaged-template fixture/loading path, so provider-registration/plugin-discovery A2 and generated/user-specific configuration override A3 remain plausible.

E1.semantic_rationale: The added fixture source shows the test helper loading the packaged user_conf_template.yml with yaml.safe_load and iterating the parsed provider mapping to generate test configuration. Under the project lead's source-aware adjudication, this removes A2 and A3; only the duplicate top-level geodes key mechanism G1 remains.

buggy_baseline.failure_signature: AssertionError: assert 'parcels' == 'output'; on the exact buggy base, the test's expected destination filename stem is 'output' but GDAL returns the source layer 'parcels'.

candidate_mechanisms.description: When dst_layer is None, the buggy copy/append call paths do not call the existing get_default_layer(dst) helper, so the missing default is delegated to GDAL/source-layer behavior instead of the destination filename stem.
candidate_mechanisms.testable_prediction: At the buggy base, default copy/append operations will not consistently use Path(dst).stem; at the fixed PR head, the same operations will use Path(dst).stem when dst_layer is None.

candidate_mechanisms.description: Only copy_layer fails to apply the default destination-layer name; append_to already applies the correct fallback.
candidate_mechanisms.testable_prediction: A frozen append_to selector with dst_layer omitted should pass on the buggy base if this is the sole cause.

candidate_mechanisms.description: Only append_to fails to apply the default destination-layer name; copy_layer already applies the correct fallback.

gold_standard.technical_rationale: The exact buggy base has a correct get_default_layer(path) helper returning Path(path).stem but does not apply it in copy_layer, append_to or _append_to_nolock when dst_layer is None. E2 eliminates copy-only and append-only explanations and narrows the format-specific alternative, but does not disclose the exact source call chain; multiple mechanisms remain, so ABSTAIN.
